gpu_mem_split.changed_because: bcm2835-codec-decode's video_decode MMAL/VCHIQ component failed to initialize at 64 MB ("Not enough GPU mem?", verified via dmesg), which is required by PROJECT SPEC section 8A/9 (real repeated hardware JPEG decode test). Temporarily raising gpu_mem to 128 in /boot/firmware/config.txt (one reboot) unblocked the hardware-JPEG-decode measurements reported in isolated/pi/jpeg-hw-decode/ and quality/.
gpu_mem_split.restoration: Per the governing task's hard restore-original-device-state requirement, the appended `gpu_mem=128` line (and its comment) was removed from /boot/firmware/config.txt after all hardware-JPEG-decode data collection was complete, and the Pi was rebooted a second time. Post-restoration verification: `vcgencmd get_mem gpu` reports `gpu=64M` (back to the original value); a full diff of the restored /boot/firmware/config.txt against the pre-benchmark snapshot showed zero differences; the gud-userspace.service descriptor log after this reboot again reports `transfer_format=rgb565 compression=1 max_buffer_size=1843200`, byte-identical to the pre-benchmark configuration.
gpu_mem_split.change_method: appended `gpu_mem=128` to /boot/firmware/config.txt, one reboot performed; later removed the same two lines and rebooted again to restore gpu_mem=64
gpu_mem_split.label: MEASURED, fully restored (see restoration note above)
gpu_mem_split.residual_impact: With gpu_mem restored to 64, bcm2835-codec-decode's video_decode component will again fail to initialize (the same 'Not enough GPU mem?' condition observed before the temporary change). Any future re-run of the hardware-JPEG-decode benchmark, or a future production rollout of the hardware-JPEG-decode candidate, needs to re-apply gpu_mem=128 (or higher) as an explicit prerequisite -- it is not a hidden permanent change, it is fully reverted.
